claims.text: The target material is a non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy.
The target alloy is in a chemically disordered state.
The alloy is suitable for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications.
A targeted enhanced-sampling algorithm can tune magnetic transition temperatures in disordered non-equiatomic HEAs.
A targeted enhanced-sampling algorithm can tune the magnitude of the magnetocaloric effect.
Monte Carlo with umbrella sampling can map the free-energy landscape governing magnetic ordering and entropy changes in the target alloy.
Chemical disorder creates subtle free-energy differences that control the balance between competing magnetic states.
Sampling the free-energy landscape can identify composition adjustments that shift the magnetic-ordering transition.
Sampling the free-energy landscape can identify microstructural adjustments that shift the magnetic-ordering transition.
The identified composition or microstructural adjustments can modify the entropy change associated with magnetic ordering.
The proposed method will produce an observable shift in magnetic transition temperature and a change in magnetocaloric entropy.
The resulting magnetocaloric change will enhance cooling performance relative to the baseline.
The relevant free-energy landscape is sufficiently sensitive to composition and microstructure under low-dimensional constraints.
Simulation predictions of the relevant free-energy landscape can correlate directly with experimental magnetic behavior.
Finite-temperature magnetic effects can influence phase stability and microstructural energetic quantities in a 3d-transition-metal HEA.
